text: A course planner, inside ChatGPT's browser. It shows what a student picked — all any timetable shows. Not what it cost them two years later, when a specialisation they wanted is quietly gone.

shot: The student does the student part
why: hold on the one free slot in term 3
text: I fill in my first year by hand. Each click is a tool call — the same tools an agent would use, tagged page, because a page can only be sure about calls it makes itself.
One slot, two courses that fit it. So I ask the page to weigh them.

why: the three lines are on screen and have to be read
text: Numerical Methods closes Graphics and Animation. Geometry closes Data and Machine Learning. Neither is free — what costs is the slot, not the course. That is reachability over a prerequisite graph under a credit budget, and nobody does it in their head.

why: 'including if you ask for it yourself', and the lock appearing
text: Now the part that runs the other way. Every rule so far belongs to the university. This one is mine.

why: the sped-up wait for the add that gets refused
text: So I ask for the course that would close it anyway.

why: highlight 'which you asked to keep open' — the shot the film is for
text: Refused — and it quotes me back to myself, not the handbook. It offers the way out and prices it: I can lift my own limit, but the specialisation goes, and it does not come back.

And that part is not really about courses. Anyone handing work to an agent has the same question, and the usual answer is a prompt — which is a request. This is a limit that outlives the conversation that set it.
All of that is on a timeline and any of it rewinds — including the limit, because a limit is an event like any other. Undo is the same reducer over fewer events.
Thirteen tools, registered with document dot modelContext dot registerTool. What shaped all of it: execute returns a string the model reads. These strings are the interface.
So a tool that changes something returns the resulting plan, never 'ok' — or the agent's picture of the state drifts from the page's.

shot: What the page will not claim
why: the end card, which is three lines to read
text: Last thing. WebMCP gives a page no way to know who called it, so this page counts calls by origin and says the attribution is a guess. That caught an assistant answering about this page correctly and in detail — having called no tool at all. It had read the repository.
